newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia must join trade organisations.
newsitem.headline: Croatia must join trade organisations.

text.p: Croatia must join European and world trade organisations to ensure a market for its products in the face of increasing competition, Economy Minister Davor Stern said on Friday.
"If Croatia remains outside the integration processes, our products will lose the competitive edge on the European market which is closing more and more," Stern told some 40 leading exporters.

He said the country hoped to secure membership of the World Trade Organisation (WTO) soon. This would ease Croatia's access to the Central European Free Trade Agreement (CEFTA) after separate deals with each of its members.

"Croatia is about to strike bilateral agreements with Slovakia, Poland and the Czech Republic this year, and we shall also solve the problem of trade and economic agreements with neighbouring Slovenia," Stern said.
Annual exports to CEFTA countries are estimated at $800 million with imports at $1.2 billion. They account for no more than between 16 and 17 percent of Croatia's foreign trade.
Its best trade partners are in the European Union, but the country has a large deficit. Stonger exports are seen as one of the keys to a proper economic recovery.
